messages:
maria: heads up — canary in us-west started degrading after the 10% traffic shift, p95 jumped to ~1.2s and error-rate to 0.9%. deploy-bot just flagged it. do we let auto-rollback run or take manual control? :thinking:

deploy-bot: ALERT: canary p95 > 900ms for 5m, error-rate > 0.5% (service=inference, model=redwood-bert-2.5.0). Suggested action: review; auto-rollback threshold met but auto-revert disabled for this change window. See /deploy/2809876543

jamal: thanks — I'm looking at traces now. latency spike seems concentrated on long-seq jobs; short ones OK. probably a kernel selection mismatch on the new quant path.

maria: can we pin traffic to previous stable until we confirm? customers in dedicated tier are on the older model but hosted traffic is impacted. need quick comms plan if we roll back. :eyes:

tess: if error-rate > 0.5% and p95 > 900ms that's our operation criteria for rollback per the Runbook (section 2.3). because auto-rollback is off, we should do a manual revert to v2.4.1 and pin. I'd prefer partial rollback (remove canary slice) first, confirm, then full rollback if still bad.

lee: +1 for staged. steps: 1) pin routing to v2.4.1 for canary slice, 2) stop traffic shift, 3) run health checks, 4) if OK release note + notify. I'll draft comms.

jamal: ok doing step 1 now. running pin command: ```
# pin canary slice back to stable
deployctl pin --env=production --slice=canary --version=v2.4.1 --reason="canary latency spike"
```

release-bot: ACTION: pin requested by jamal. Pin will apply in ~15s. Change window: rolling. Audit: link=/audit/2809876543

maria: once pin completes we stop the shift and monitor for 10m. if p95 returns to baseline and errors drop <0.3% we keep and follow up with a rollback note in release notes. if not, escalate to full rollback.

tess: monitoring: running smoke tests and trace sampling. results so far (2m): p95 down to 420ms, errors 0.12%. dropping fast.

jamal: good — canceling roll-forward for the rest of the slices. command: ```
# cancel remaining traffic steps
deployctl rollout --id=2809800000 --action=hold
```

maria: comms: I'll post a short update to #customer-briefing and notify the account team for big Dedicated customers. Lee, please add a short entry in the release notes: "Canary traffic reverted from redwood-bert-2.5.0 to v2.4.1 due to p95 regression on long-sequence workload; investigation ongoing."

lee: on it. also adding a follow-up ticket for runtime/quant-kernel team to reproduce with long-seq traces: TKT-1429.

jamal: retrospective actions: 1) add kernel fallback in runtime to avoid whole canary spike, 2) validate quant path on long sequences in CI, 3) consider enabling auto-rollback for low-risk canary slices. adding to postmortem.

maria: thanks team. closing thread when release-bot confirms pin completed and canary stable for 15m. tagging @sre-oncall for visibility. :white_check_mark:

release-bot: Pin applied. canary slice now at v2.4.1. Monitoring window started.

tess: 15m check-in: stable. p95 steady, no error spikes. marking done and moving to postmortem doc.

maria: good job — will send consolidated comms after postmortem draft.
